profile.headline: Embedded Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I am a security-focused software developer with a desire to work at the cutting edge of the industry. I love solving intricate and detail-oriented problems and have a passion for systems that keep users and businesses protected in a volatile digital landscape.

I graduated from Oregon State University in June of 2023, with BS in Computer Science, along with a Certificate in Cybersecurity and a Minor in Mathematics.
Some of my most Relevant Classes include:
 - Technical Writing
 - Operating Systems: I & II
 - Cryptography
 - Analysis of Algorithms
 - Software Engineering: I & II
 - Computer Architecture & Assembly Language

I also have experience using:
 - C, C++, C#, Swift, PHP, MASM, & Python
 - OpenMP, OpenCL, OpenGL, & CUDA
 - Visual Studio, Xcode, & Vim
 - AWS Console/API for IAM, Lambda, APIGateway & S3 
 - Conan, Jira, Reviewboard, & Github
 - Linode, Docker, Zapier, Postman, Unity Engine, VMware Workstation & LaTex

positions.title: Mecop Intern
positions.description:
This was an exciting jump into embedded software development. Over the course of this internship, I had the opportunity to work on a team spanning multiple engineering disciplines and learn from all of them. Alongside speed-focused, close-to-the-hardware programming, I also experienced working in an ITAR-compliant environment, and the greater attention to detail required.
Here I also:
- Coordinated with Electrical and Mechanical Engineers to drive smooth software integration
- Rapidly prototyped software to evaluate 5 SoC and microcontroller hardware alternatives
- Independently sought & solved future hurdles, reducing tech debt by 90% with 25+ bug fixes
- Created and maintained 20+ pages of documentation for internal tools, hardware, and processes

positions.title: Mecop Intern
positions.description:
Through the Mecop Program, I had the opportunity to intern with VMware Carbon Black. Here I worked with an incredibly talented team and mentor in R&D for the Windows Carbon Black Cloud Sensor.
The most important skill I picked up during this internship was the ability to integrate with an existing codebase. Carbon Black has a massive codebase, and, in order to begin working on the team, I had to step into the middle of what had already been written. Through the internship, I saw a huge improvement in my ability to cohesively understand code written by others, and decipher the many moving parts of a large application.
Some of my accomplishments included:
- Integrated with the agile team remotely to contribute to a large system software code base
- Built and grafted a preprocessor script into the continuous integration pipeline
- Increased application debugging speed by 10% via refactoring internal logging
- Programmed for Windows User & Kernel mode, including driver development

positions.title: Intern App and Web Developer
positions.description:
Developed the DialTalkDone Podcasting App
● Integrated between five different cloud services
● Programmed and debugged the application workflow
● Created the user account system
● Managed and applied feedback from beta-testers and the Apple App portal
● Started, scripted, and updated the Linux server and AWS services
● Delivered internal and external documentation and technical support
Developed the Premiumcast Podcast Publishing System
● Integrated new features with longstanding company systems and workflows
● Drafted internal documentation.

volunteerExperiences.description: At the Antioch house, I was elected, as the Community Service Chair. From this position, I collaborated with the leadership team and led the house in giving back to our community. This meant finding service opportunities and connecting our 47 members with the needs of our community.
